title: attendance
description: One person in one class, in one role, and where they stand: the record that puts someone in a class. Assigning a person to a class creates this record (starting assigned); withdrawing, attending, being late and the rest are later statuses on the same record, kept in status_history. Students and instructors are both attendance records. A class's roster is read from the records for that class; a person's history is read from the records for that person. Nothing here is stored twice. Rules the schema cannot express: the individual exists and is not erased; the class exists and is not deleted; one live record per individual per class; individual_id and scheduled_class_id never change; status defaults to assigned (or waitlisted for a student when the class is full) and each status is added to status_history.
x_retention: Kept as history after a class has run. When the individual is erased the record is soft deleted and everything that describes it is removed, leaving an anonymous tombstone. (A written policy only; nothing enforces it yet.)

individual_id.description: The person: the id of an individual. Required. Must exist and not be erased (a merged person is followed to the survivor). Never changes once set.

scheduled_class_id.description: The class: the id of a scheduled_class. Required. Must exist and not be deleted. Never changes once set. A person has one live record per class.

role.description: What the person is in this class: student, primary_instructor or instructor (a secondary instructor). Required.

order.description: The place among the instructors, 1 first: a whole number from 1 to 50. For instructors only; optional.

status.description: Where the person stands: assigned (the operator placed them), waitlisted (the class was full), confirmed (they said they are coming), attended, late, no_show, declined (they said no), withdrawn (they left) or cancelled (the class or the booking was cancelled). Optional on create (the server uses assigned, or waitlisted for a student when the class is full); every change is added to status_history. Reviews are a separate record, not a status.

status_history.description: Every status the record has had, oldest first: the status, when it was set, and who set it. Set by the server whenever status is set or changed. Up to 100 entries.

by.description: Who set it, as an actor string.

correspondence.description: DEPRECATED (CMS refactor, October 15, 2026): no longer written or read by the server; the message log (communication_log) replaced it. Kept so older records stay valid; to be removed from the schema after the test-data cleanup. Every message the system sent about this placement, oldest first: a small log. Each line says when it was sent (UTC), what kind it was, the channel, the address it went to, the subject, how it came out, and who or what sent it. The message text is not kept. Set by the server only (the Console never writes it); a record with no lines has had no messages. Up to 100 entries.

at.description: When it was sent or tried (UTC).

kind.description: What the message was: placement_confirmation (you are scheduled, with the calendar file).

to.description: The address it was sent to.

result.description: sent (the mail service accepted it; this is not proof of delivery), failed (it was not sent; see error_code) or unknown (the connection ended before we could tell).

error_code.description: A short sanitized reason when result is failed or unknown (for example missing_key or recipient_rejected). Never contains personal data.

by.description: Who triggered it, as an actor string: the person who placed them, or who pressed Send.

trigger.description: automatic (sent when the person was placed) or manual (someone pressed Send confirmation email).

request_id.description: The registration request this record came from, when it came from one: the id of a registration_request. Optional. When set, the server copies that request's confirmation_number onto this record. A request counts as placed while at least one record carrying its id is not declined, withdrawn or cancelled.

confirmation_number.description: The confirmation number of the registration request this record came from (ICDT- followed by six characters), copied from the request by the server when request_id is set, so the request can be traced from the class. Read only. Optional. This is the request's number, not this record's own: see reference_number.

reference_number.description: This person's own reference for this class, ICDT-A- followed by six characters (no vowels, no 0 or 1). Set by the server on every new record, whether or not it came from a request, and never changes. Read only. Records made before this field existed do not have one.

notes.description: Free text for the operator about this person in this class. Up to 2000 characters. Personal data. Optional.

id.description: UUID v4, set by the server; also the Firestore document id.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the record was written under (currently 2). Set by the server.

created_at.description: When the record was created (UTC). Set by the server.

created_by.description: Who created it, as an actor string. Set by the server.

updated_at.description: When the record last changed (UTC). Set by the server.

updated_by.description: Who last changed it. Set by the server.

source.description: Where the record came from: dashboard or import. Set by the server.

deleted_at.description: When the record was soft deleted (UTC); absent while live. A deleted link is a mistake corrected, not a relationship that ended. Set by the server.

deleted_by.description: Who soft deleted it. Set by the server.
